body.en:
Unix is a multi-user, multitasking operating system developed in 1969 at AT&T Bell Labs by Ken Thompson and Dennis Ritchie. It was rewritten in the C language in 1973, which made it portable to many machines.

Linux is a free and open-source, Unix-like operating system. Its kernel was created in 1991 by Linus Torvalds, a student in Finland. The Linux kernel combined with GNU tools (bash, gcc, coreutils) forms a complete OS, often called GNU/Linux. A distribution (distro) packages the kernel, tools, desktop and installer: Ubuntu, Fedora, Debian, Linux Mint, Red Hat, Kali.

Features of Linux

  • Free and open source: source code is available under the GPL; anyone can study, modify and distribute it.
  • Multi-user: many users can use the system at the same time, each with their own account.
  • Multitasking: many programs run concurrently.
  • Portable: runs on PCs, servers, phones (Android), routers and supercomputers.
  • Security: user accounts, file permissions (rwx), root/superuser separation.
  • Hierarchical file system: everything starts from the root /; devices are also files.
  • Shell and utilities: powerful command line with hundreds of small commands that can be combined using pipes.
  • Networking support built in; stable and reliable; little need for antivirus.

body.en:
The Unix/Linux system is organised in layers around the hardware. Each layer uses the services of the layer inside it.

1. Hardware

The innermost layer: CPU, memory, disks, terminals and other devices.

2. Kernel

The heart of the OS; it is loaded into memory at boot and runs in kernel (privileged) mode. It interacts directly with the hardware and provides services to programs through system calls (fork, exec, open, read, write).

  • Process management (creation, scheduling, termination, IPC)
  • Memory management (allocation, paging, swapping)
  • File management (file system, permissions)
  • Device management (device drivers, I/O)
  • Networking and security

3. Shell

The command interpreter and the interface between the user and the kernel. It reads commands typed by the user, interprets them and asks the kernel to execute the programs. It also provides a programming language (shell scripts).

4. Utilities and application programs

Commands and programs used by users: ls, cp, grep, sort, vi, gcc, editors, compilers, browsers, databases.

5. Users

Users interact with the system through the shell or a graphical desktop.

h.en: 5.1.3 Linux System Structure and Programming Basics
h.gu: 5.1.3 Linux System Structure અને Programming Basics

body.en:
Linux system structure (user space and kernel space)

  • User space: applications, shell and system utilities, and system libraries (glibc) that wrap system calls into functions such as printf(), fopen().
  • System call interface: the only entry from user space into the kernel.
  • Kernel space: the Linux kernel is monolithic but supports loadable kernel modules (drivers can be added at run time).

Programming basics

Programming on Unix/Linux is based on a few simple ideas:

  • Everything is a file: ordinary files, directories, devices (/dev/sda, /dev/tty) and even processes (/proc) are accessed like files.
  • Small tools, combined: each command does one job well; commands are joined with pipes (|) and redirection (>, <).
  • Text streams: every program has three standard files: stdin (0, keyboard), stdout (1, screen) and stderr (2, screen).
  • Processes: a new process is created with fork() and a new program is loaded with exec(); each process has a PID (ps, kill).
  • Users and permissions: every file has an owner, a group and rwx permissions; root is the superuser.
  • Programming tools: shell scripts (bash), editors (vi, vim, gedit, nano), the C compiler gcc, make, debugger gdb; also Python, Java and more.

Logging in

The user logs in with a user name and password; the shell then shows a prompt such as student@pc:~$ (# for root). Commands are typed after the prompt and executed when Enter is pressed. exit or Ctrl+D logs out.

Unix/Linux પર programming થોડા સરળ વિચારો પર આધારિત છે:

  • બધું જ file છે: સામાન્ય files, directories, devices (/dev/sda, /dev/tty) અને processes (/proc) પણ files ની જેમ access થાય છે.
  • નાના tools, જોડીને: દરેક command એક કામ સારી રીતે કરે છે; commands pipes (|) અને redirection (>, <) વડે જોડાય છે.
  • Text streams: દરેક program પાસે ત્રણ standard files હોય: stdin (0, keyboard), stdout (1, screen) અને stderr (2, screen).
  • Processes: નવી process fork() થી બને અને નવો program exec() થી load થાય; દરેક process ને PID હોય (ps, kill).
  • Users અને permissions: દરેક file ને owner, group અને rwx permissions હોય; root superuser છે.
  • Programming tools: shell scripts (bash), editors (vi, vim, gedit, nano), C compiler gcc, make, debugger gdb; ઉપરાંત Python, Java વગેરે.

Login

User user name અને password થી login કરે; પછી shell student@pc:~$ જેવો prompt બતાવે (root માટે #). Commands prompt પછી type કરાય અને Enter દબાવતાં ચાલે. exit અથવા Ctrl+D logout કરે.

body.en:
All files in Linux are arranged in a single inverted tree that starts at the root directory /. There are no drive letters as in Windows; other disks and pen drives are mounted on a directory of this tree (e.g. /media/usb). The layout follows the Filesystem Hierarchy Standard (FHS).

DirectoryContents
/Root of the whole file system
/bin, /sbinEssential user and system commands (ls, cp, mount)
/bootKernel image and boot loader (GRUB) files
/devDevice files: /dev/sda (disk), /dev/tty (terminal), /dev/null
/etcSystem configuration files: passwd, group, hosts, fstab
/homeHome directories of users (/home/student)
/libShared libraries and kernel modules
/rootHome directory of the superuser root
/tmpTemporary files, cleared at reboot
/usrUser programs and data: /usr/bin, /usr/lib, /usr/share
/varVariable data: logs (/var/log), mail, spool
/mnt, /mediaMount points for other file systems, pen drives
/procVirtual files with process and kernel information

Each user has a home directory (/home/student, written as ~) where the shell starts after login; users can create files only there (and in /tmp). Path names can be absolute (/etc/passwd) or relative (../notes.txt).

/bin, /sbinજરૂરી user અને system commands (ls, cp, mount)

body.en:
The shell is a program that provides the command-line interface to Linux. It is both a command interpreter (runs commands typed by the user) and a programming language (shell scripts with variables, conditions and loops).

Types of shells

ShellProgramNotes
Bourne shellshOriginal Unix shell (Stephen Bourne); prompt $
Bourne Again shellbashDefault on most Linux systems; history, completion
C shellcsh / tcshC-like syntax; prompt %
Korn shellkshCombines sh and csh features
Z shellzshDefault on macOS; powerful completion

echo $SHELL shows the current shell; cat /etc/shells lists the available shells.

How the shell executes a command

  1. Displays the prompt and reads the command line.
  2. Parses it into command, options and arguments; expands wildcards (*, ?, [ ]), variables ($x) and command substitution.
  3. Finds the command: a built-in (cd, echo, pwd) or an external program searched in the directories of $PATH.
  4. Creates a child process (fork), runs the program in it (exec) and waits; then shows the prompt again.

Command format

command [options] [arguments] e.g. ls -l /home. Options usually start with - and can be combined (ls -la). Commands are case-sensitive. Help: man ls, ls --help.

Redirection, pipes and wildcards

  • > output to a file (overwrite), >> append, < input from a file, 2> errors to a file.
  • | pipe: output of one command becomes input of the next.
  • * any characters, ? one character, [abc] one of the listed characters.
  • Quotes: "…" expands variables, '…' does not.

Example (real output)

$ echo $SHELL
/bin/bash
$ echo Hello > h.txt
$ echo World >> h.txt
$ cat h.txt
Hello
World
$ wc -l < h.txt
2
$ ls | wc -l
3
$ ls *.txt
a.txt  h.txt
$ name=Ravi; echo "Hi $name"
Hi Ravi
$ echo 'Hi $name'
Hi $name

  • | pipe: એક command નું output આગળના command નું input બને.
  • * કોઈ પણ અક્ષરો, ? એક અક્ષર, [abc] યાદીમાંનો એક અક્ષર.
  • Quotes: "…" variables expand કરે, '…' નહીં.

ઉદાહરણ (ખરું output)

$ echo World >> h.txt
$ cat h.txt

$ wc -l < h.txt
2

3

a.txt  h.txt

h.en: 5.2.2 Directory Commands: pwd, cd, mkdir, rmdir, ls
h.gu: 5.2.2 Directory Commands: pwd, cd, mkdir, rmdir, ls

body.en:
pwd (print working directory)

Displays the absolute path of the current directory. Syntax: pwd

cd (change directory)

Changes the current directory. cd dir, cd .. (parent), cd / (root), cd or cd ~ (home), cd - (previous directory). Both absolute and relative paths can be used.

mkdir (make directory)

Creates one or more directories: mkdir os, mkdir d1 d2. Option -p creates the whole path including missing parents: mkdir -p sem3/os/unit5.

rmdir (remove directory)

Removes empty directories only: rmdir os. A non-empty directory gives an error; use rm -r to delete it with its contents.

ls (list)

Lists the files and directories. Common options:

  • -l long listing (permissions, links, owner, group, size, date, name)
  • -a all files including hidden ones (names starting with .)
  • -R recursive (subdirectories too), -t sort by time, -r reverse, -i inode number, -h human-readable sizes, -d directory itself

Example (real output)

$ pwd
/home/student
$ mkdir os
$ mkdir -p sem3/os/unit5
$ ls
notes.txt  os  prog.c  sem3
$ ls -a
.   .profile   os      sem3
..  notes.txt  prog.c
$ ls -l

$ cd sem3/os
$ pwd

$ cd ..
$ pwd
/home/student/sem3
$ cd ~
$ rmdir os
$ ls -R sem3

os

sem3/os:
unit5

rmdir: failed to remove 'sem3': Directory not empty

h.en: 5.2.3 File Commands: cat, cp, rm, mv
h.gu: 5.2.3 File Commands: cat, cp, rm, mv

body.en:
cat (concatenate)

  • cat file displays a file; cat f1 f2 displays several files one after another.
  • cat > file creates a file from keyboard input (end with Ctrl+D); cat >> file appends.
  • cat f1 f2 > f3 joins files into f3; -n numbers the lines.

cp (copy)

  • cp src dest copies a file; cp f1 f2 dir/ copies files into a directory.
  • -r copies directories recursively, -i asks before overwriting, -p preserves time and permissions.

rm (remove)

  • rm file deletes files permanently (no recycle bin).
  • -i asks for confirmation, -r deletes a directory and everything in it, -f forces without asking. rm -rf must be used very carefully.

mv (move / rename)

  • mv old new renames a file or directory.
  • mv file dir/ moves it into another directory (the inode is unchanged, so moving within the same file system is instant).
  • -i asks before overwriting.

Example (real output)

$ cat a.txt
Operating System
Linux commands
$ cat -n a.txt b.txt
     1	Operating System
     2	Linux commands

cat (concatenate)

  • cat file file બતાવે; cat f1 f2 ઘણી files એક પછી એક બતાવે.
  • cat > file keyboard input થી file બનાવે (Ctrl+D થી પૂરું); cat >> file append કરે.
  • cat f1 f2 > f3 files ને f3 માં જોડે; -n lines ને નંબર આપે.

cp (copy)

  • cp src dest file copy કરે; cp f1 f2 dir/ files ને directory માં copy કરે.
  • -r directories ને recursively copy કરે, -i overwrite પહેલાં પૂછે, -p time અને permissions જાળવે.

rm (remove)

  • rm file files ને કાયમ માટે delete કરે (recycle bin નથી).
  • -i ખાતરી માંગે, -r directory અને તેમાંનું બધું delete કરે, -f પૂછ્યા વગર force કરે. rm -rf ખૂબ સાવધાનીથી વાપરવું.

mv (move / rename)

  • mv old new file કે directory નું નામ બદલે.
  • mv file dir/ તેને બીજી directory માં ખસેડે (inode બદલાતો નથી, તેથી એ જ file system માં move તરત થાય).
  • -i overwrite પહેલાં પૂછે.

wc (word count)

Counts lines, words and characters (bytes) of a file. Output order: lines, words, bytes, file name. Options: -l lines only, -w words, -c bytes, -m characters. With a pipe: ls | wc -l counts files.

split

Splits a large file into smaller pieces named xaa, xab, … (or with a given prefix). Default: 1000 lines per piece. -l n n lines per piece, -b size by bytes (1k, 1m). The pieces can be joined back with cat part_* > file.

head

Displays the first lines of a file (default 10). head -n 3 file or head -3 file; -c for bytes.

tail

Displays the last lines of a file (default 10). tail -n 2 file; tail -n +5 file from line 5 to the end; tail -f log keeps showing new lines as the file grows (used for log files).

Combined: head -7 file | tail -3 shows lines 5 to 7.

Example (real output)

Priya IT 92
Amit CE 65

Anjali IT 73
$ split -l 4 students.txt part_
$ ls
part_aa  part_ab  part_ac  students.txt
$ cat part_ac
Vivek ME 67
Anjali IT 73

h.gu: 5.2.5 Files ની સરખામણી: cmp, comm, diff

body.en:
cmp (compare)

Compares two files byte by byte and reports the first difference (byte number and line number). If the files are identical it prints nothing and returns exit status 0. Works for binary files too. -l lists all differing bytes.

comm (common)

Compares two sorted files line by line and prints three columns:

  1. lines only in file 1,
  2. lines only in file 2 (one tab),
  3. lines common to both (two tabs).

-1, -2, -3 suppress the corresponding column; comm -12 f1 f2 shows only common lines.

diff (difference)

Shows all line differences and tells what changes are needed to make file 1 identical to file 2. Codes: a add, c change, d delete; lines from file 1 are marked < and lines from file 2 >. Example: 3c3 means line 3 of f1 must be changed to line 3 of f2. Options: -i ignore case, -w ignore white space, -u unified format.

Example (real output)

$ cat f1.txt
apple
banana
cherry
mango
$ cat f2.txt
apple
banana
grape
mango
orange
$ cmp f1.txt f2.txt
f1.txt f2.txt differ: byte 14, line 3
$ cmp f1.txt f1.txt && echo same
same
$ comm f1.txt f2.txt
		apple
		banana
cherry
	grape
		mango
	orange
$ comm -12 f1.txt f2.txt
apple
banana
mango
$ diff f1.txt f2.txt
3c3
< cherry
---
> grape
4a5
> orange

cmp (compare)

બે files ને byte દર byte સરખાવે અને પહેલો તફાવત (byte number અને line number) જણાવે. Files સરખી હોય તો કંઈ છાપતું નથી અને exit status 0 આપે. Binary files માટે પણ કામ કરે. -l બધા જુદા bytes ની યાદી આપે.

comm (common)

બે sorted files ને line દર line સરખાવે અને ત્રણ columns છાપે:

  1. માત્ર file 1 માંની lines,
  2. માત્ર file 2 માંની lines (એક tab),
  3. બંનેમાં સામાન્ય lines (બે tabs).

-1, -2, -3 અનુરૂપ column છુપાવે; comm -12 f1 f2 માત્ર સામાન્ય lines બતાવે.

બધા line તફાવતો બતાવે અને file 1 ને file 2 જેવી બનાવવા કયા ફેરફારો જોઈએ તે કહે. Codes: a add, c change, d delete; file 1 ની lines < અને file 2 ની lines > થી દર્શાવાય. ઉદાહરણ: 3c3 એટલે f1 ની line 3 ને f2 ની line 3 માં બદલવી. Options: -i case અવગણો, -w white space અવગણો, -u unified format.

apple
banana
cherry
mango
$ cat f2.txt
apple
banana
grape
mango
orange

f1.txt f2.txt differ: byte 14, line 3

same
$ comm f1.txt f2.txt

body.en:
grep (Global Regular Expression Print)

Searches files for lines that match a pattern and prints them. Syntax: grep [options] pattern [files]

  • -i ignore case, -v print lines that do not match, -c count matching lines, -n show line numbers, -l list only file names, -w whole word, -e several patterns.
  • Regular expressions: ^ start of line, $ end of line, . any character, * zero or more, [abc] one of. Example: grep '^A' file lines starting with A.

sort

Sorts the lines of a file (default: alphabetical, ascending) and prints them; the file itself is not changed unless -o is used.

  • -r reverse, -n numeric, -u remove duplicates, -f ignore case.
  • -k n sort by field n, -t ':' field separator (e.g. sort -t: -k3 -n /etc/passwd).
  • -o file write the result to a file.

Example (real output)

File students.txt has 10 lines of the form name branch marks.

$ grep CE students.txt
Ravi CE 78
Amit CE 65
Karan CE 71
Pooja CE 95
$ grep -i ravi students.txt
Ravi CE 78
$ grep -c CE students.txt
4
$ grep -v -e CE -e IT students.txt

Arjun EE 59
Vivek ME 67
$ grep -n '^A' students.txt

7:Arjun EE 59
10:Anjali IT 73
$ grep -l Ravi *.txt
notes.txt
students.txt
$ sort students.txt | head -4
Amit CE 65
Anjali IT 73
Arjun EE 59
Karan CE 71
$ sort -r students.txt | head -3
Vivek ME 67
Sneha IT 84
Ravi CE 78
$ sort -k3 -n students.txt | head -3
Arjun EE 59
Amit CE 65
Vivek ME 67
$ sort -k3 -nr students.txt | head -3
Pooja CE 95
Priya IT 92
Neha ME 88
$ cut -d' ' -f2 students.txt | sort | uniq -c
      4 CE
      1 EE
      3 IT
      2 ME

title.gu: 5.3 Files Editing: vi, vim, gedit અને gcc

body.en:
vi (visual editor) is the standard screen-oriented text editor available on every Unix/Linux system; it works in a terminal without a mouse. vim (vi improved) is an enhanced version with syntax highlighting, multi-level undo, split windows, tabs and plugins. On most Linux systems the vi command actually starts vim.

Start: vi notes.txt or vim notes.txt (creates the file if it does not exist).

Modes of vi

  1. Command mode (normal mode): the default mode when vi starts. Keys act as commands: move the cursor, delete, copy, paste, undo.
  2. Insert mode: entered by i, a, o, I, A, O; whatever you type is inserted into the file. Press Esc to return to command mode.
  3. Last-line (ex / command-line) mode: entered by typing : in command mode; the cursor moves to the bottom line for commands like save, quit, search-replace and settings. Enter executes the command.

Important vi commands

TaskCommand (in command mode)
Inserti (before cursor), a (after), o (new line below), I, A, O
Moveh j k l (left, down, up, right), w / b word, 0 / $ line start / end, gg / G first / last line, :n go to line n
Deletex character, dw word, dd line, 3dd three lines, D to end of line
Copy / pasteyy copy line, 3yy three lines, p paste below, P above
Undo / redou undo, Ctrl+R redo, . repeat last change
Search / replace/word forward, ?word backward, n next, :%s/old/new/g replace all
Save / quit:w save, :w name save as, :q quit, :wq or ZZ save and quit, :q! quit without saving
Settings:set nu line numbers, :set nonu, :syntax on (vim)

Typical session: vi hello.sh → press i → type the script → Esc → :wq → Enter.

vi (visual editor) એ દરેક Unix/Linux system પર ઉપલબ્ધ standard screen-oriented text editor છે; તે mouse વગર terminal માં કામ કરે છે. vim (vi improved) syntax highlighting, multi-level undo, split windows, tabs અને plugins વાળું સુધારેલું version છે. મોટા ભાગની Linux systems માં vi command ખરેખર vim શરૂ કરે છે.

શરૂ કરવા: vi notes.txt અથવા vim notes.txt (file ન હોય તો બનાવે).

body.en:
gedit is the default graphical (GUI) text editor of the GNOME desktop (Ubuntu, Fedora). It is easy to use, like Notepad on Windows, with menus and mouse support.

  • Start: gedit file.txt & from the terminal (& runs it in the background so the terminal remains free), or from the applications menu.
  • Features: syntax highlighting for C, Python, shell, HTML; line numbers; multiple tabs; search and replace (Ctrl+H); spell check; undo/redo; plugins.
  • Shortcuts: Ctrl+N new, Ctrl+O open, Ctrl+S save, Ctrl+Shift+S save as, Ctrl+F find, Ctrl+Q quit.

vi vs gedit

  • vi works in any terminal (also over SSH, without a GUI); gedit needs a graphical desktop.
  • vi is mode-based and keyboard-driven; gedit is modeless and mouse-friendly, easier for beginners.
  • Other editors: nano (simple terminal editor), emacs, VS Code.

h.gu: 5.3.3 gcc વડે C Programs Compile કરવા

body.en:
gcc (GNU Compiler Collection) is the standard compiler for C (and C++) on Linux. A C program is written with an editor (vi / gedit), compiled with gcc and run from the shell.

Steps

  1. Write the program: vi hello.c (or gedit hello.c).
  2. Compile: gcc hello.c creates the executable a.out; gcc hello.c -o hello names it hello.
  3. Run: ./a.out or ./hello (./ because the current directory is not in PATH).
  4. If there are errors, gcc shows the file name, line number and message; edit and compile again.

Stages of compilation

  • Preprocessing (gcc -E): handles #include and #define → .i
  • Compilation (gcc -S): C to assembly → .s
  • Assembly (gcc -c): assembly to object code → .o
  • Linking: joins object files and libraries (printf from libc) → executable

Useful options

-o name output file, -Wall show all warnings, -g debugging information (for gdb), -lm link the math library (for sqrt, pow), -c compile only.

Example (real output)

$ cat hello.c
#include <stdio.h>
int main()
{
    printf("Hello, Linux!\n");
    return 0;
}
$ gcc hello.c
$ ls
a.out  hello.c
$ ./a.out
Hello, Linux!
$ gcc hello.c -o hello
$ ./hello
Hello, Linux!
body.gu:
gcc (GNU Compiler Collection) એ Linux પર C (અને C++) માટેનો standard compiler છે. C program editor (vi / gedit) થી લખાય, gcc થી compile થાય અને shell માંથી ચલાવાય.

પગલાં

  1. Program લખો: vi hello.c (અથવા gedit hello.c).
  2. Compile: gcc hello.c executable a.out બનાવે; gcc hello.c -o hello તેને hello નામ આપે.
  3. ચલાવો: ./a.out અથવા ./hello (./ કારણ કે current directory PATH માં નથી).
  4. Errors હોય તો gcc file name, line number અને message બતાવે; સુધારી ફરી compile કરો.

Compilation ના તબક્કા

  • Preprocessing (gcc -E): #include અને #define સંભાળે → .i
  • Compilation (gcc -S): C થી assembly → .s
  • Assembly (gcc -c): assembly થી object code → .o
  • Linking: object files અને libraries (libc નું printf) જોડે → executable

ઉપયોગી options

-o name output file, -Wall બધી warnings, -g debugging માહિતી (gdb માટે), -lm math library link (sqrt, pow માટે), -c માત્ર compile.

h.en: 5.4.1 Shell Script Basics: Variables, echo, read
h.gu: 5.4.1 Shell Script Basics: Variables, echo, read

body.en:
A shell script is a text file containing a sequence of shell commands, along with variables, conditions and loops. It is used to automate repetitive tasks (backups, installations, reports).

Writing and running a script

  1. Create the file: vi first.sh
  2. First line #!/bin/bash (the shebang) tells which interpreter runs it; # starts a comment.
  3. Run with bash first.sh or sh first.sh; or give execute permission chmod +x first.sh and run ./first.sh.
#!/bin/bash
# my first shell script
echo "Today is a good day"
echo -n "Enter your name: "
read name
echo "Hello, $name"

Variables

  • User-defined: name=Ravi, n=10 (no spaces around =; no data types, all values are strings). Use with $: echo $name or ${name}.
  • System (environment) variables: $HOME, $PATH, $USER, $SHELL, $PWD.
  • readonly x makes a constant; unset x removes a variable.

echo and read

  • echo "text $var" prints; -n no newline; -e enables \n, \t.
  • read var reads a line from the keyboard; read a b c reads several words; read -p "Prompt: " x shows a prompt.

Quotes and command substitution

  • "…" double quotes: variables are expanded. '…' single quotes: everything literal. \ escapes one character.
  • today=$(date) or `date` stores the output of a command.
body.gu:
Shell script એ variables, conditions અને loops સાથેના shell commands નો ક્રમ ધરાવતી text file છે. તેનો ઉપયોગ પુનરાવર્તિત કાર્યો (backups, installations, reports) automate કરવા થાય છે.

Script લખવી અને ચલાવવી

  1. File બનાવો: vi first.sh
  2. પહેલી line #!/bin/bash (shebang) કહે કે કયો interpreter ચલાવશે; # comment શરૂ કરે.
  3. bash first.sh અથવા sh first.sh થી ચલાવો; અથવા execute permission આપો chmod +x first.sh અને ./first.sh ચલાવો.
#!/bin/bash
# my first shell script
echo "Today is a good day"
echo -n "Enter your name: "
read name
echo "Hello, $name"

Variables

  • User-defined: name=Ravi, n=10 (= ની આસપાસ spaces નહીં; data types નથી, બધી કિંમતો strings છે). $ સાથે વાપરો: echo $name અથવા ${name}.
  • System (environment) variables: $HOME, $PATH, $USER, $SHELL, $PWD.
  • readonly x constant બનાવે; unset x variable દૂર કરે.

echo અને read

  • echo "text $var" છાપે; -n newline નહીં; -e \n, \t ચાલુ કરે.
  • read var keyboard માંથી line વાંચે; read a b c ઘણા શબ્દો વાંચે; read -p "Prompt: " x prompt બતાવે.

Quotes અને command substitution

  • "…" double quotes: variables expand થાય. '…' single quotes: બધું શાબ્દિક. \ એક અક્ષરને escape કરે.
  • today=$(date) અથવા `date` command નું output રાખે.

body.en:
Values can be passed to a script on the command line after its name: bash add.sh 40 60. Inside the script they are available as positional parameters.

VariableMeaning
$0Name of the script
$1 … $9, ${10}First to ninth (tenth…) argument
$#Number of arguments
$@All arguments as separate words ("$@")
$*All arguments as a single string ("$*")
$?Exit status of the last command (0 = success)
$$Process ID (PID) of the current shell

Points to remember

  • Always check $# and print a usage message if the arguments are missing.
  • shift shifts the arguments left: $2 becomes $1, and $# decreases by 1 (useful in loops).
  • set a b c sets the positional parameters inside a script.
  • exit 0 ends the script successfully; a non-zero value indicates an error (seen by the caller in $?).
body.gu:
Script ના નામ પછી command line પર કિંમતો આપી શકાય: bash add.sh 40 60. Script ની અંદર તે positional parameters તરીકે મળે છે.

Variableઅર્થ
$0Script નું નામ
$1 … $9, ${10}પહેલાથી નવમો (દસમો…) argument
$#Arguments ની સંખ્યા
$@બધા arguments અલગ શબ્દો તરીકે ("$@")
$*બધા arguments એક string તરીકે ("$*")
$?છેલ્લા command નો exit status (0 = success)
$$હાલના shell નો Process ID (PID)

યાદ રાખવાના મુદ્દા

  • હંમેશા $# તપાસો અને arguments ખૂટતા હોય તો usage message છાપો.
  • shift arguments ને ડાબે ખસેડે: $2 એ $1 બને, અને $# 1 ઘટે (loops માં ઉપયોગી).
  • set a b c script ની અંદર positional parameters set કરે.
  • exit 0 script ને સફળતાપૂર્વક પૂરી કરે; non-zero કિંમત error દર્શાવે (caller ને $? માં દેખાય).

body.en:
Shell variables hold strings, so arithmetic must be done with expr, $(( )) or let. Only integer arithmetic is supported (use bc for decimals: echo "5/2" | bc -l).

Arithmetic operators

OperatorMeaningexpr form$(( )) form
+Additionexpr $a + $b$((a + b))
-Subtractionexpr $a - $b$((a - b))
*Multiplicationexpr $a \* $b$((a * b))
/Integer divisionexpr $a / $b$((a / b))
%Remainder (modulus)expr $a % $b$((a % b))
=Assignmenta=10 (no spaces)let a=b+1

With expr, spaces around operators are required and * must be escaped (\*).

Relational operators (for numbers)

OperatorMeaningExample (a=10, b=20)
-eqequal to[ $a -eq $b ] → false
-nenot equal to[ $a -ne $b ] → true
-gtgreater than[ $a -gt $b ] → false
-gegreater than or equal[ $a -ge 10 ] → true
-ltless than[ $a -lt $b ] → true
-leless than or equal[ $b -le 15 ] → false

Inside (( )) the C-style operators == != > >= < <= can be used: if (( a > b )).

Logical operators

OperatorMeaningExample
-aAND (inside [ ])[ $a -gt 0 -a $a -lt 100 ]
-oOR (inside [ ])[ $x -eq 1 -o $x -eq 2 ]
!NOT[ ! -f file ]
&&AND between commands[ $a -gt 0 ] && [ $a -lt 100 ]
||OR between commands[ -f f ] || echo "missing"

Shell variables strings રાખે છે, તેથી arithmetic expr, $(( )) કે let થી કરવું પડે. માત્ર integer arithmetic support છે (decimals માટે bc: echo "5/2" | bc -l).

Arithmetic operators

Operatorઅર્થexpr સ્વરૂપ$(( )) સ્વરૂપ

-બાદબાકીexpr $a - $b$((a - b))
*ગુણાકારexpr $a \* $b$((a * b))
/Integer ભાગાકારexpr $a / $b$((a / b))
%શેષ (modulus)expr $a % $b$((a % b))
=Assignmenta=10 (spaces નહીં)let a=b+1

expr સાથે operators ની આસપાસ spaces જરૂરી અને * ને escape (\*) કરવો પડે.

Relational operators (સંખ્યાઓ માટે)

Operatorઅર્થઉદાહરણ (a=10, b=20)

-neબરાબર નથી[ $a -ne $b ] → true
-gtથી મોટું[ $a -gt $b ] → false
-geથી મોટું કે બરાબર[ $a -ge 10 ] → true
-ltથી નાનું[ $a -lt $b ] → true
-leથી નાનું કે બરાબર[ $b -le 15 ] → false

(( )) ની અંદર C-style operators == != > >= < <= વાપરી શકાય: if (( a > b )).

Logical operators

Operatorઅર્થઉદાહરણ
-aAND ([ ] ની અંદર)[ $a -gt 0 -a $a -lt 100 ]

h.en: 5.4.4 Evaluating Expressions with the test Command

body.en:
The test command evaluates a condition and returns an exit status: 0 (true) if the condition holds and 1 (false) otherwise. It prints nothing; it is used with if, while, && and ||.

Two equivalent forms: test $a -gt $b and [ $a -gt $b ]. In the bracket form, spaces after [ and before ] are compulsory. bash also has [[ … ]], which allows &&, || and pattern matching inside.

Types of tests

TypeTestTrue if
Strings1 = s2 / s1 != s2strings are equal / not equal
String-z s / -n sstring is empty / not empty
File-e ffile exists
File-f f / -d fregular file / directory
File-r f -w f -x freadable / writable / executable
File-s ffile exists and size > 0
Number-eq -ne -gt -ge -lt -lenumeric comparison (see relational operators)

Examples

  • test -f notes.txt && echo "exists"
  • [ "$ans" = "yes" ] (quote variables so an empty value does not cause an error)
  • [ -d backup ] || mkdir backup
  • test 5 -eq 5; echo $? prints 0 (true).
body.gu:
test command શરત મૂલવે છે અને exit status આપે છે: શરત સાચી હોય તો 0 (true) અને નહીં તો 1 (false). તે કંઈ છાપતું નથી; તે if, while, && અને || સાથે વપરાય છે.

બે સરખા સ્વરૂપ: test $a -gt $b અને [ $a -gt $b ]. Bracket સ્વરૂપમાં [ પછી અને ] પહેલાં spaces ફરજિયાત છે. bash માં [[ … ]] પણ છે, જે અંદર &&, || અને pattern matching મંજૂર કરે છે.

Tests ના પ્રકારો

પ્રકારTestક્યારે true
Strings1 = s2 / s1 != s2strings સરખી / જુદી
String-z s / -n sstring ખાલી / ખાલી નથી
File-e ffile છે
File-f f / -d fregular file / directory
File-r f -w f -x freadable / writable / executable
File-s ffile છે અને size > 0
Number-eq -ne -gt -ge -lt -lenumeric સરખામણી (relational operators જુઓ)

ઉદાહરણો

  • test -f notes.txt && echo "exists"
  • [ "$ans" = "yes" ] (variables ને quote કરો જેથી ખાલી કિંમતથી error ન આવે)
  • [ -d backup ] || mkdir backup
  • test 5 -eq 5; echo $? 0 (true) છાપે.

body.en:
The if statement executes commands depending on the exit status of a condition (usually a test). If the status is 0 (true), the then part runs.

Forms

  • Simple if: run commands only when the condition is true.
  • if-else: choose between two blocks.
  • if-elif-else (ladder): test several conditions in turn; the first true block runs.
  • Nested if: an if inside another if.
# simple if
if [ $n -gt 0 ]
then
  echo "Positive"
fi

# if-else
if [ $n -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "Positive"
else
  echo "Not positive"
fi

# if-elif-else ladder
if [ $n -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "Positive"
elif [ $n -lt 0 ]; then
  echo "Negative"
else
  echo "Zero"
fi

Rules

  • then must be on a new line or after ;.
  • Every if ends with fi (if written backwards).
  • Spaces inside [ ] are required: [ $a -gt $b ], not [$a -gt $b].
body.gu:
if statement શરત (સામાન્ય રીતે test) ના exit status મુજબ commands ચલાવે છે. Status 0 (true) હોય તો then ભાગ ચાલે.

સ્વરૂપો

  • Simple if: શરત સાચી હોય ત્યારે જ commands ચલાવો.
  • if-else: બે blocks માંથી એક પસંદ કરો.
  • if-elif-else (ladder): ઘણી શરતો વારાફરતી તપાસો; પહેલો સાચો block ચાલે.
  • Nested if: એક if ની અંદર બીજું if.
# simple if
if [ $n -gt 0 ]
then
  echo "Positive"
fi

# if-else
if [ $n -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "Positive"
else
  echo "Not positive"
fi

# if-elif-else ladder
if [ $n -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "Positive"
elif [ $n -lt 0 ]; then
  echo "Negative"
else
  echo "Zero"
fi

નિયમો

  • then નવી line પર કે ; પછી હોવું જોઈએ.
  • દરેક if fi (if ઊંધું) થી પૂરું થાય.
  • [ ] ની અંદર spaces જરૂરી: [ $a -gt $b ], [$a -gt $b] નહીં.

body.en:
The case statement is a multi-way branch, a cleaner alternative to a long if-elif ladder when one value is compared with many patterns (menus, choices).

case $var in
  pattern1) commands ;;
  pattern2|pattern3) commands ;;
  *) default commands ;;
esac

Working

  • The value of $var is compared with each pattern from top to bottom.
  • The commands of the first matching pattern run up to ;;, then control goes to esac.
  • *) matches anything and acts as the default; it is written last.
  • Patterns may use wildcards: [aeiou], [0-9], [a-z]*, and | for alternatives (y|Y|yes)).
  • The statement ends with esac (case written backwards).
body.gu:
case statement multi-way branch છે; એક કિંમતને ઘણા patterns સાથે સરખાવવાની હોય (menus, choices) ત્યારે લાંબા if-elif ladder નો સ્વચ્છ વિકલ્પ છે.

case $var in
  pattern1) commands ;;
  pattern2|pattern3) commands ;;
  *) default commands ;;
esac

કાર્યપદ્ધતિ

  • $var ની કિંમત ઉપરથી નીચે દરેક pattern સાથે સરખાવાય.
  • પહેલા મેળ ખાતા pattern ના commands ;; સુધી ચાલે, પછી control esac પર જાય.
  • *) કંઈ પણ સાથે મેળ ખાય અને default તરીકે કામ કરે; તે છેલ્લે લખાય.
  • Patterns માં wildcards વાપરી શકાય: [aeiou], [0-9], [a-z]*, અને વિકલ્પો માટે | (y|Y|yes)).
  • Statement esac (case ઊંધું) થી પૂરું થાય.

body.en:
A loop repeats a set of commands. The while loop repeats the body as long as the condition is true (exit status 0). It is used when the number of repetitions is not known in advance.

i=1
while [ $i -le 5 ]
do
  echo $i
  i=`expr $i + 1`
done

# until: repeats while condition is FALSE
until [ $i -gt 5 ]; do ...; done

Working

  1. Initialise the loop variable (i=1).
  2. Test the condition; if false, jump after done.
  3. Execute the body between do and done.
  4. Update the variable (otherwise the loop never ends), then go back to step 2.

Loop control

  • break exits the loop immediately; continue skips to the next iteration.
  • while true or while : creates an infinite loop (stop with break or Ctrl+C).
  • while read line; do … done < file reads a file line by line.
body.gu:
Loop commands ના સમૂહને ફરી ફરી ચલાવે છે. while loop શરત સાચી રહે ત્યાં સુધી (exit status 0) body ફરી ચલાવે છે. પુનરાવર્તનોની સંખ્યા અગાઉથી ખબર ન હોય ત્યારે વપરાય.

i=1
while [ $i -le 5 ]
do
  echo $i
  i=`expr $i + 1`
done

# until: repeats while condition is FALSE
until [ $i -gt 5 ]; do ...; done

કાર્યપદ્ધતિ

  1. Loop variable initialise કરો (i=1).
  2. શરત તપાસો; ખોટી હોય તો done પછી જાઓ.
  3. do અને done વચ્ચેની body ચલાવો.
  4. Variable update કરો (નહીં તો loop ક્યારેય પૂરો ન થાય), પછી step 2 પર પાછા.

Loop control

  • break loop માંથી તરત બહાર નીકળે; continue આગળના iteration પર જાય.
  • while true અથવા while : infinite loop બનાવે (break કે Ctrl+C થી બંધ).
  • while read line; do … done < file file ને line દર line વાંચે.

body.en:
The for loop executes the body once for each item in a list; the loop variable takes the items one by one. It is used when the items (or the count) are known.

for name in list
do
  commands
done

for i in 1 2 3 4 5     # list of words
for i in {1..10}       # range
for f in *.txt         # file names
for x in "$@"          # all arguments
for (( i=1; i<=5; i++ ))   # C-style

Working

  1. The first item of the list is assigned to the variable.
  2. The body between do and done runs.
  3. The next item is assigned and the body runs again, until the list is finished.

while vs for

  • while: condition-controlled; the variable must be updated by the programmer.
  • for: list-controlled; the shell assigns each item automatically.
  • Both support break and continue and end with done.
body.gu:
for loop યાદીની દરેક item માટે એક વાર body ચલાવે છે; loop variable items ને એક પછી એક લે છે. Items (કે સંખ્યા) ખબર હોય ત્યારે વપરાય.

for name in list
do
  commands
done

for i in 1 2 3 4 5     # list of words
for i in {1..10}       # range
for f in *.txt         # file names
for x in "$@"          # all arguments
for (( i=1; i<=5; i++ ))   # C-style

કાર્યપદ્ધતિ

  1. યાદીની પહેલી item variable ને અપાય.
  2. do અને done વચ્ચેની body ચાલે.
  3. આગળની item અપાય અને body ફરી ચાલે, યાદી પૂરી થાય ત્યાં સુધી.

while vs for

  • while: condition-controlled; variable programmer એ update કરવો પડે.
  • for: list-controlled; shell દરેક item આપમેળે આપે.
  • બંને break અને continue support કરે અને done થી પૂરા થાય.

code.en:
#!/bin/bash

q.en: What is Linux?
q.gu: Linux શું છે?

a.en: A free, open-source, Unix-like operating system kernel created by Linus Torvalds in 1991; with GNU tools it forms a complete OS.
a.gu: 1991 માં Linus Torvalds એ બનાવેલું free, open-source, Unix-like operating system kernel; GNU tools સાથે સંપૂર્ણ OS બને છે.

q.en: Name some Linux distributions.
q.gu: કેટલાંક Linux distributions જણાવો.

a.en: Ubuntu, Fedora, Debian, Linux Mint, Red Hat Enterprise Linux, Kali, Arch.
a.gu: Ubuntu, Fedora, Debian, Linux Mint, Red Hat Enterprise Linux, Kali, Arch.

q.en: What is the kernel?
q.gu: Kernel શું છે?

a.en: The core of the OS that manages processes, memory, files and devices and talks directly to the hardware.
a.gu: OS નો મુખ્ય ભાગ જે processes, memory, files અને devices નું સંચાલન કરે છે અને hardware સાથે સીધો વાત કરે છે.

q.en: What is a shell?
q.gu: Shell શું છે?

a.en: A command interpreter that reads user commands and asks the kernel to execute them (sh, bash, csh, ksh).
a.gu: Command interpreter જે user ના commands વાંચે છે અને kernel ને તેમને ચલાવવા કહે છે (sh, bash, csh, ksh).

q.en: What is the root directory?
q.gu: Root directory શું છે?

a.en: The top of the Linux file hierarchy, written as /. (root is also the name of the superuser.)
a.gu: Linux file hierarchy નું ટોચનું સ્થાન, / તરીકે લખાય. (root superuser નું નામ પણ છે.)

q.en: What is a hidden file?
q.gu: Hidden file શું છે?

a.en: A file whose name starts with a dot (e.g. .profile); shown only by ls -a.
a.gu: જેનું નામ dot થી શરૂ થાય તેવી file (દા.ત. .profile); માત્ર ls -a થી દેખાય.

q.en: Difference between rmdir and rm -r?
q.gu: rmdir અને rm -r વચ્ચે તફાવત?

a.en: rmdir removes only an empty directory; rm -r removes a directory with all its contents.
a.gu: rmdir માત્ર ખાલી directory દૂર કરે; rm -r directory ને તેની બધી સામગ્રી સાથે દૂર કરે.

q.en: Difference between > and >>?
q.gu: > અને >> વચ્ચે તફાવત?

a.en: > redirects output to a file, overwriting it; >> appends to the end of the file.
a.gu: > output ને file માં redirect કરી overwrite કરે; >> file ના અંતે append કરે.

q.en: What is a pipe?
q.gu: Pipe શું છે?

a.en: The | symbol sends the output of one command as input to the next, e.g. ls | wc -l.
a.gu: | ચિહ્ન એક command નું output આગળના command ને input તરીકે મોકલે, દા.ત. ls | wc -l.

q.en: Difference between cmp and diff?
q.gu: cmp અને diff વચ્ચે તફાવત?

a.en: cmp reports the first differing byte; diff lists all line differences and how to change one file into the other.
a.gu: cmp પહેલો જુદો byte જણાવે; diff બધા line તફાવતો અને એક file ને બીજી જેવી કેવી રીતે બનાવવી તે બતાવે.

q.en: What does comm need and show?
q.gu: comm ને શું જોઈએ અને શું બતાવે?

a.en: Two sorted files; it shows lines only in file 1, only in file 2, and common to both in three columns.
a.gu: બે sorted files; તે ત્રણ columns માં માત્ર file 1 માં, માત્ર file 2 માં અને બંનેમાં સામાન્ય lines બતાવે.

q.en: What does grep stand for?
q.gu: grep નું પૂરું નામ?

a.en: Global Regular Expression Print: it prints lines that match a pattern.
a.gu: Global Regular Expression Print: pattern સાથે મેળ ખાતી lines છાપે.

q.en: How do you sort numerically in reverse?
q.gu: Numeric reverse sort કેવી રીતે કરશો?

a.en: sort -nr file (use -k to choose a field).
a.gu: sort -nr file (field પસંદ કરવા -k વાપરો).

q.en: What are the modes of vi?
q.gu: vi ના modes કયા છે?

a.en: Command mode (default), insert mode (i, a, o) and last-line/ex mode (:).
a.gu: Command mode (default), insert mode (i, a, o) અને last-line/ex mode (:).

q.en: How do you save and quit vi?
q.gu: vi માં save અને quit કેવી રીતે?

a.en: :wq or ZZ; :q! quits without saving.
a.gu: :wq અથવા ZZ; :q! save કર્યા વગર quit કરે.

q.en: Difference between vi and vim?
q.gu: vi અને vim વચ્ચે તફાવત?

a.en: vim (vi improved) adds syntax highlighting, multi-level undo, split windows and plugins.
a.gu: vim (vi improved) syntax highlighting, multi-level undo, split windows અને plugins ઉમેરે છે.

q.en: What is the default output file of gcc?
q.gu: gcc ની default output file કઈ?

a.en: a.out; use -o name to choose another name.
a.gu: a.out; બીજું નામ આપવા -o name વાપરો.

q.en: What is a shell script?
q.gu: Shell script શું છે?

a.en: A text file containing a sequence of shell commands with variables, conditions and loops, executed by the shell.
a.gu: Variables, conditions અને loops સાથેના shell commands નો ક્રમ ધરાવતી text file, જે shell ચલાવે છે.

q.en: What is the shebang line?
q.gu: Shebang line શું છે?

a.en: The first line #!/bin/bash, telling the system which interpreter runs the script.
a.gu: પહેલી line #!/bin/bash, જે system ને કહે કે કયો interpreter script ચલાવશે.

q.en: What are $#, $@ and $?

a.en: $# number of arguments, $@ all arguments, $? exit status of the last command (0 = success).
a.gu: $# arguments ની સંખ્યા, $@ બધા arguments, $? છેલ્લા command નો exit status (0 = success).

q.en: Why is * escaped in expr?
q.gu: expr માં * ને escape શા માટે કરાય?

a.en: Otherwise the shell expands * to the list of file names before expr sees it.
a.gu: નહીં તો expr સુધી પહોંચે તે પહેલાં shell * ને file names ની યાદીમાં ફેરવી દે.

q.en: What is the test command?
q.gu: test command શું છે?

a.en: It evaluates an expression (numeric, string or file test) and returns exit status 0 for true; [ ] is its short form.
a.gu: તે expression (numeric, string કે file test) મૂલવે છે અને સાચું હોય તો exit status 0 આપે; [ ] તેનું ટૂંકું સ્વરૂપ છે.

q.en: How do you end if, case, while and for?
q.gu: if, case, while અને for કેવી રીતે પૂરા કરશો?

a.en: if … fi, case … esac, while … do … done, for … do … done.
a.gu: if … fi, case … esac, while … do … done, for … do … done.
